key_messages: After a few showers this morning, drier conditions return this afternoon through early Monday.
Shower and thunderstorm chances return later Monday through early Tuesday as a weak front moves through the region.
Unsettled weather continues for the latter half of the week ahead, with temperatures trending slightly below normal by the weekend.

Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
640 AM EDT Sun Aug 9 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 226 AM EDT Sunday...

Precipitation chances across south-central Vermont have
increased this morning with an area of showers tracking through
from west to east.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 236 AM EDT Sunday...
1. After a few showers this morning, drier conditions return
this afternoon through early Monday. 

2. Shower and thunderstorm chances return later Monday through
early Tuesday as a weak front moves through the region.

3. Unsettled weather continues for the latter half of the week 
ahead, with temperatures trending slightly below normal by the 
weekend.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 236 AM EDT Sunday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Showers are tracking across the southern
Adirondacks into south-central Vermont this hour and will
continue to move through over the morning hours. While a rumble
of thunder cannot be completely ruled out. Another area of
instability is moving through southern Canada towards the 
border. Isolated to scattered showers are possible in this area 
through the morning with a few thunderstorms possible by noon. 
Coverage will be decreasing by mid-afternoon with drier 
conditions moving into the region through Monday. Temperatures 
will again be warm today, but a degree or so cooler than 
yesterday with highs in the mid/upper 70s to low/mid 80s.

KEY MESSAGE 2: A front will approach late Monday bringing more
widespread chances of showers and thunderstorms. However, flow
aloft will be increasingly zonal resulting in weaker surface
features and less forcing along the boundary. So, strong storms
are not very likely. Winds behind the front will align with Lake
Champlain supporting rough lake conditions late Monday into
Tuesday. Another dry period is likely Tuesday afternoon through
Wednesday with temperatures and RH continuing to slowly 
decrease. Highs around 80 degrees with dew points in the 50s 
will feel like a treat compared to recent muggy conditions. 

KEY MESSAGE 3: Unsettled weather is expected to continue through the 
second half of next week, with chances for showers and thunderstorms 
and an overall trend towards cooler temperatures towards the 
weekend. Zonal flow across the region will allow for several quick 
shortwaves to move through, bringing chances for showers although 
the progressive flow will limit hydro concerns. As of now, Thursday 
looks to be the day with the greatest chances for showers, with some 
possible thunderstorms in the afternoon. Of course, the timing of 
any of these shortwaves and shower chances may chance as we get 
closer. Looking towards the end of the week, the upper-level flow 
will amplify as ridging builds over the western US with downstream 
troughing over the eastern US/Canada. The cyclonic flow over the 
northeastern US will favor a continuation of scattered showers with 
slightly below normal temperatures for the weekend.

&&

.AVIATION /12Z SUNDAY THROUGH THURSDAY/...
Through 12Z Monday...Once fog and lower clouds dissipate across
the region this morning, VFR conditions are expected to prevail
throughout most of the forecast period. A few isolated to
scattered showers may be possible this morning, but drier
weather is expected by the afternoon through the rest of the
forecast period. Winds will generally be light throughout the 
TAF period, with increasing westerly winds expected in the 
afternoon with a few gusts possible. Additional fog development
may be possible at some of the favored locations towards the end
of the forecast period, but left mention of it out of the TAF
for now. 

Outlook...

Monday: VFR. Chance SHRA, Slight chance TSRA.
Monday Night: Mainly VFR, with local IFR possible. Likely SHRA,
Slight chance TSRA.
Tuesday: Mainly VFR, with local IFR possible. Slight chance SHRA,
Slight chance TSRA.
Tuesday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Wednesday: VFR. Slight chance SHRA, Slight chance TSRA.
Wednesday Night: VFR. Slight chance SHRA.
Thursday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. Chance SHRA,
Chance TSRA.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&

$$

DISCUSSION...Boyd/Kremer
AVIATION...Kremer
